private_benchmark_comparison.method: Six relevant private gameplay views were reviewed sequentially as unlabeled A/B pairs. Candidate and benchmark order was randomized independently with system entropy before inspection. Each source retained its original aspect ratio by fit-with-padding; there was no crop, stretch, or retouch. Candidate identity and order were revealed only after each judgment. Temporary extraction and temporary pair renders were deleted, and no private pixels or source-identifying names or paths were copied into the repository.

scorecard.scale: 0-10 per category; ten named categories sum directly to 100

categories.finding: The compact leading fold remains clear and substantially faithful, with minor generative surface drift.
Identity, stance, framing, and blade mass mostly hold, but the hilt and pommel-tail construction drift outside scope.
The low outside bend is candidate04's decisive and immediately visible improvement.
The shoulder-to-elbow limb is overlong and hose-like, and the low bend lacks a convincing joint structure.
A reversal exists but is too short, shallow, and visually fused with the hilt to carry the intended counterforce.
The hand remains on a hilt-like form but has moved far outward and down from the authoritative inward grip.
No qualifying empty arm-bounded triangle exists.
Both hands contact one apparent weapon, but the altered bent tail and hilt-limb collision break frozen construction and load clarity.
The low bend survives reduction, but the return, hand placement, and wedge do not read without explanation.
The illustration is polished concept evidence, but it clears only two focused comparisons and lacks benchmark-grade anatomy, force continuity, and gameplay integration.
